E1.evidence: Public issue #551 (title 'QoS compatibility failing silently (ROS2)') gives a three-step reproducer ('Run a ROS2 node that publishes data to a topic using **Best Effort** reliability. ... Run `rosbridge_server` and attempt to subscribe to that topic using a rosbridge client library (roslibpy, roslibjs). The subscriber should not receive any data. ... Change the reliability policy on the publisher to **Reliable** and repeat step 2. The subscriber should now receive data from the publisher.'), a log excerpt, and the environment ('ROS Version (`echo $ROS_DISTRO`): foxy', 'Rosbridge Version ...: 1.0.2 (more specifically 1a2c386)'). Maintainer jtbandes (MEMBER) confirmed and closed it: 'Should be fixed by #690'. PR #690 body states 'Fixes #551'.

E2.evidence: Step 1: the two units are rosbridge_library (package in RobotWebTools/rosbridge_suite that creates the ROS 2 subscription on behalf of the rosbridge_websocket node from rosbridge_server; separate package.xml files, same repository) and the reporter's ROS 2 publisher node on /my_topic, which the report does not name. Step 2 (not internal): the subscription's declared QoS is the unit's boundary; at the broken revision rosbridge_library/src/rosbridge_library/internal/subscribers.py line 107-108 reads '# TODO(@jubeira): add support for other QoS.' / 'self.subscriber = node_handle.create_subscription(msg_class, topic, self.callback, 10)', i.e. depth only, default (reliable) reliability. The fix (PR #690) changes that declaration: it builds 'qos = QoSProfile(depth=10, durability=DurabilityPolicy.VOLATILE, reliability=ReliabilityPolicy.RELIABLE)', calls 'infos = node_handle.get_publishers_info_by_topic(topic)' and sets 'qos.reliability = ReliabilityPolicy.BEST_EFFORT' when 'any(pub.qos_profile.reliability == ReliabilityPolicy.BEST_EFFORT for pub in infos)', then passes qos to create_subscription. Step 3 (not deployment wiring): no remap, namespace, topic or parameter renaming is involved. Step 4 (not build): no build-system or dependency change. Step 5 (not firmware). Step 6: eligible; the interface is a topic whose two endpoints declared incompatible reliability QoS.

E3.evidence: PAIR: the publisher's output on the topic feeds rosbridge's subscription input. Reproducer: 'Run a ROS2 node that publishes data to a topic using **Best Effort** reliability.' then 'Run `rosbridge_server` and attempt to subscribe to that topic'. No other operation is supported by the source.

E4.evidence: Observed outcome in the issue: 'The `rosbridge_server` logs indicate that the client connected and that the subscription was created, but no data is ever received in the subscriber callback.'

failed_conditions.quote: `rosbridge_server` silently fails to subscribe to topics with publishers that use **Best Effort** reliability instead of **Reliable.** The `rosbridge_server` logs indicate that the client connected and that the subscription was created, but no data is ever received in the subscriber callback.

loudness_evidence: The only diagnostics shown are the successful-looking rosbridge log lines '[INFO] [1611352924.485146047] [rosbridge_websocket]: Client connected. 1 clients total.' and '[INFO] [1611352926.636802670] [rosbridge_websocket]: [Client 1] Subscribed to /my_topic'; the reporter states 'it would seem that a failure to connect based on QoS compatibility either fails silently or requires more verbose logging than I currently have configured.' No ROS 2 incompatible-QoS event appears in the source.

resolution.summary: In rosbridge_library, when creating a subscription, query node_handle.get_publishers_info_by_topic(topic) and set the subscription's reliability to BEST_EFFORT if any existing publisher on the topic uses BEST_EFFORT (and durability to TRANSIENT_LOCAL if any publisher uses TRANSIENT_LOCAL), instead of the fixed default profile (depth 10, reliable, volatile).
resolution.evidence: PR #690 'Allow subscribing to any qos profile when creating a subscriber' (merged 2021-12-09, merge commit adfa4d6335462e321d774400a6ffbf285cb28531, first release tag containing it: 1.1.1) states 'Subscriber QoS is automatically chosen based on available publishers to achieve compatible QoS settings in more cases.' and 'Fixes #551'. It adds the launch test rosbridge_server/test/websocket/best_effort_publisher.test.py, which creates 'QoSProfile(reliability=ReliabilityPolicy.BEST_EFFORT, history=HistoryPolicy.SYSTEM_DEFAULT)' publisher on /a_topic, subscribes through rosbridge and asserts receipt of '[{"op": "publish", "topic": "/a_topic", "msg": {"data": "hello"}}]'. The maintainer's closing comment is 'Should be fixed by #690'. The source contains no run record of the resolved composition (GitHub reports 0 check runs and a 'pending' combined status for the merge commit) and no confirmation from the reporter, so the status is recorded as recommended rather than observed.

notes: Unit naming: the ROS node in the graph is rosbridge_websocket from package rosbridge_server; the subscription QoS declaration and the fix live in rosbridge_library, which rosbridge_server imports; both packages are versioned together in RobotWebTools/rosbridge_suite (package.xml version 1.0.2 at 1a2c386, 1.1.0 at adfa4d6; 1a2c386 is 'Adaptations to Eloquent [Again] (#533)', 2020-09-19, ros2 branch). The provider unit is the reporter's own node and is not named; the only concrete best-effort publisher in the source is the rclpy test publisher added by PR #690 in rosbridge_server/test/websocket/best_effort_publisher.test.py. The reporter originally attributed the failure to custom message definitions and edited the issue ('it turns out that the problem was actually regarding ROS2 QoS settings'). Message type on /my_topic is not stated. PR #690 also adopts TRANSIENT_LOCAL durability when a publisher has it (motivated by latched /tf_static messages not reaching rosbridge, https://github.com/ros2/ros2cli/issues/523#issuecomment-987107534); that is a separate qos_durability condition not observed in #551 and is listed here only as context. Earlier attempts closed by #690: PR #582 (qos_durability parameter) and PR #654 (query publisher QoS; its 'How to test' shows a different, tier4-fork implementation receiving a 'ros2 topic pub --qos-reliability best_effort' publisher on galactic, and a comment reports a Foxy error 'Failed to create subscription: Unknown QoS history policy' for a SYSTEM_DEFAULT-history variant; #690 keeps depth=10). Known limitation stated in the fix: 'more publishers may come online after our subscriber is set up'. Resolved-composition ros_distro is not stated in the PR (ros2 branch); 'foxy' is the reporter's environment. Confidence is medium because the provider unit is unnamed and the resolved composition is not shown running in the source.
